title: Keep completion feed productive and account for material still maturing
statement: Under the separate instantaneous model e_dot=-A*e^3 with A>0,e0>0, e(t)=[e0^(-2)+2*A*t]^(-1/2)>0 for finite t; reaching positive tolerance eps<e0 takes [eps^(-2)-e0^(-2)]/(2*A). A positive minimum productive flow can stop growth earlier. Separately, for fixed eta in[0,1], tau>0 and z_dot=q-z/tau, d_dot=eta*z/tau, d+eta*z changes at rate eta*q. If feed stops at t*, eventual d is d(t*)+eta*z(t*), assuming all remaining stock follows this maturation law. With total subsequent feed <=B, d_final<=d0+eta*(z0+B).

body: Integrate d(e^-2)/dt=2*A to obtain the cubic closure law. It models opening proportional to remaining stiffness error, laminar slit flow proportional to opening cubed and instantaneous conversion to useful repair; it is not the delayed-stock model. A positive tolerance is attainable in finite model time, so asymptotic exact equality alone does not prove failure of every useful repair target. Maintenance thresholds or finite resources require their actual laws. For the delayed model, differentiate d+eta*z; the maturation terms cancel. After q=0, z=z(t*)*exp[-(t-t*)/tau] and the stated remaining stock contributes eta*z(t*). The finite-budget bound follows by integrating q and taking nonnegative remaining stock. This analytic consequence was reconstructed from the supplied ODE and code; it is not a reproduced numerical trajectory. q,z,d use calibrated source-normalized stiffness-equivalent units and eta is fixed useful conversion; real mass, attachment and orientation need their own mapping. The two-stage mechanical gate can choose q using calibrated comparator signs, but source final stiffnesses and noisy repair populations remain reports. Feedback detects missing function; it cannot make eta positive or create a missing load-bearing attachment.
